scope: Portable linguistic assessments and the separately identified contextual provider-responsibility policy.

rules.title: Interrogative versus indefinite pronoun accent
conditions: The candidate lemma is exactly τίς or τις.
The original surface has a listed spelling.
The following token, if supplied, is the immediately following word before any punctuation boundary.
rules.effect: Return a score contribution for an existing candidate; never select or rewrite a lemma.
exceptions: Acute monosyllabic τί/τίς before a possible enclitic: abstain.
Contracted τοῦ/τῷ and unlisted forms: not applicable.
Written accents may be editorial or erroneous; this is defeasible evidence.
The following-enclitic list is finite and is not a complete contextual analysis.

parameters.weight_status: Uncalibrated engineering choices, not values supplied by Smyth.

rules.title: Apostrophe equivalence and word boundaries
conditions: A configured apostrophe-like mark appears in Greek text.
rules.effect: Unify supported apostrophe spellings; preserve prodelision and distinguish token boundaries.
exceptions: Do not conflate Greek numeral marks, genuine breathings or a coronis with apostrophes.

rules.title: Crasis candidate generation
conditions: A table entry, structural prefix or internal coronis supports a candidate split.
An automatic restoration requires local morphological evidence for the inflected form or an explicit inflected restoration in the project inventory.
Generated vowel and accent variants are used for lookup. A headword hint or a model prediction alone does not establish the restored form.

ὦ fused with a vocative not listed in the crasis table (ὦναίσχυντε = ὦ ἀναίσχυντε, ὦταῖρε = ὦ ἑταῖρε): only when the written form has no analysis of its own and a restoration with a smoothly or roughly breathed α/ε/ο (or the existing contraction rules) has a Diogenes analysis in the vocative or nominative. Owner request, 24 November 2026.
rules.effect: Pass supported inflected readings to the models. When no split is supported, keep the written token and its whole-word analyses and flag unresolved crasis.
exceptions: Initial diphthong breathings are not medial coronides.
Keep recognised prefixed verbs such as προὔδωκεν whole.
Lexical internal aspiration, e.g. ταὧσι, has explicit exceptions.
Initial crasis, e.g. ἅνδρες, needs separate evidence.

sources.title: Smyth, Greek Grammar
sources.supports: Crasis, coronis and accent conventions. The evidence gate is an application decision.

sources.title: Aristophanes, Acharnians 82
sources.supports: The written form κἄχεζεν. The local Morpheus analysis supplies χέζω for the whole form.

sources.title: Project crasis table and lexical exceptions; entry-level provenance incomplete

counterexamples: ὦμος, ὦτα, ὦσι and ὤμοι have analyses of their own and stay single words; ὦλεκτρυόν stays unrestored because Diogenes lacks the vocative ἀλεκτρυόν.

rules.title: Elision and prodelision restoration candidates
conditions: An initial or final elision mark is present.
Full forms have local lexical support or an explicit table hint.
rules.effect: Generate alternatives subject to phonological/grammatical checks and restoration penalties.
exceptions: Final -αι requires supported verbal morphology.
Final -οι is restricted rather than an arbitrary restoration.
Rare dative -ι restoration remains penalised and visible for review.
Unresolved restorations retain a warning.

rules.title: Lexical and contextual grammar agreement
conditions: A candidate and contextual tag have explicit comparable features.
rules.effect: Add agreement/conflict weights; preserve original feature alternatives as evidence.
exceptions: Missing features supply no matching evidence.
VERB/AUX and CCONJ/SCONJ have defined equivalences.

sources.title: Application scoring policy; weights are not a grammatical theorem

rules.title: Provider priors and neural score floor
conditions: The hybrid ranker receives a candidate and its provider score.
rules.effect: Combine provider priors with clipped neural scores; this entry describes only these terms, not the complete ranker.
exceptions: Other ranker terms, including structural hints, function words and agreement, also affect selection.

sources.title: Application engineering policy, not externally validated linguistic evidence

rules.title: Prioritise lemma/segmentation doubts
conditions: Stored readings and observations are available.
Unresolved contextual output, a shortened context, or an ambiguous-form model lookup fallback is explicitly flagged in the contextual pipeline.
Unresolved standard-headword mappings and provisional Diogenes dictionary associations are urgent review observations; selected lemmata are not changed by the review policy.
A capitalised lemma on a lower-case written form (grc.grammar.proper-noun abstention) is an urgent review observation.
Generated lemmata replaced from the same text or removed for an impossible spelling (grc.selection.generated-lemma-check) are urgent review observations.
rules.effect: Flag unresolved/unsupported analyses or close alternatives with different lemmas/segmentation; do not change the selected lemma.
exceptions: Same-lemma grammatical alternatives are secondary observations.
A distant unsupported GreTa alternative alone does not make a local winner doubtful.

sources.title: Application review policy; no calibrated error-rate claim

rules.title: Preserve indefinite/interrogative distinction during optional normalisation
conditions: Optional accent normalisation is enabled and the form is τὶ or τὶς.
rules.effect: Normalise to unaccented τι/τις rather than interrogative τί/τίς, preserving letter case.
exceptions: Do not change an original acute interrogative.

rules.title: Separate suffixed headwords for deictic iota
conditions: Surface spelling belongs to the finite documented inventory, including case, NFC/NFD and grave/acute variants.
Selected provider lemma belongs to the matching base/deictic family.
Apply after provider selection, before manual corrections. Do not change ranking scores or raw proposals.
rules.effect: Return the suffixed family headword and a deictic suffix annotation, retaining one token. The caller applies the proposal.
exceptions: Unknown forms and unaccented spellings: no proposal; never strip or append iota generically.
Unrelated or missing selected lemma: abstain and retain the original selection for review.
Intercalated particles such as γε/δέ/μέν/γάρ are outside this inventory.
Original spelling, POS, provider evidence and scores are not rewritten.
Existing saved analyses keep their stored decisions on replay. Explicit manual corrections take precedence.

sources.title: Smyth, Greek Grammar
sources.supports: Deictic suffix, demonstrative inflectional families and adverb examples; not the export headword policy.

sources.title: LSJ, οὗτος
sources.supports: Explicit strengthened forms, including τουτῳί, τουτονί, οὑτοιί and ταυτί.

rules.title: Corroborated form and headword part of speech
conditions: Apply after lemma and expansion ranking to a selected candidate with no explicit grammatical class.
The form and selected headword both have local Morpheus evidence.
Every class represented in each source inventory is explicit, and both inventories agree on one class.
For verbal classes every local form analysis must explicitly have VerbForm=Fin.
An incompatible or missing selected part of speech can be replaced. Existing compatible functional labels are retained.
rules.effect: Return a proposed POS and clear_msd=true when corroborated. The backend changes the final POS and clears inherited features. Lemma, expansion, raw provider data and ranking scores stay outside this policy.
exceptions: Unknown classes, including X, missing evidence, multiple classes or disagreement cause abstention.
Participles, infinitives and unspecified verbal forms cause abstention because function can depend on context.
VERB/AUX and the existing indeclinable compatibility groups are accepted.
Dictionary inventories can be incomplete. Evidence from two views of Morpheus is corroboration within one source, not independent provider agreement.
Exact dictionary headword spelling is required in this backend. Unsupported spellings abstain.
OGA imports and previously saved decisions are outside automatic application.
counterexamples: A form with verbal and nominal analyses.
A headword whose inventory contains an unknown class.
A participle used adjectivally.
An infinitive used substantivally.
A particle with a compatible contextual ADV label.

sources.supports: Use corroborated part of speech and document the decision after assessing removal of spaCy/OdyCy.

rules.title: Contextual disambiguation and explicit provider responsibilities
conditions: Lexical input is the current atom's complete, isolated Diogenes/explicit-restoration lemma inventory.
One distinct local lemma is retained; GreBERTa joint selects among ambiguous or unseen forms.
With two or more local lemmata, a contextual proposal is accepted only if it is one of them (case and grave/acute ignored; breathings, other accents and diaeresis significant).
Otherwise, when the model-owned UPOS-conditioned canonical lookup supplies one of the local lemmata, it is accepted (`context_outside_inventory_lookup`).

Failing canonical lookup, the contextual model's ranked top-k edit-script candidates (when supplied) are checked and the highest-probability in-inventory candidate is accepted (`context_topk_inventory_disambiguation`), except when top-1 is already an attested headword of the whole local morphology (`known_lemma`) and the top-k candidate lags top-1 by more than `topk_known_headword_max_gap` (2.5) log-probability units.
Failing top-k, GreTa may supply one of the local lemmata; failing that, the proposal is kept only if it is an attested headword of the whole local morphology, else the policy abstains.
The contextual adapter records keep-aware neural-first decoding, top-k contextual candidates, and explicit model-owned lookup fallbacks.
When no contextual proposal resolves an ambiguous/unseen form (and top-k yields no local candidate), GreTa can supply a labelled helper proposal.
rules.effect: Return a selected lemma and provenance trace without modifying provider evidence. No provider voting or GreTa candidate rescoring. A generated string cannot replace an available local inventory.
exceptions: Morpho is additional evidence and reviewer lookup, with no automatic selection vote.
A unique lemma with a weak dictionary link is not thereby verified or rejected; link quality remains separate.
No resolved proposal and no unique lexical/helper lemma: abstain and retain all candidates.
Original inflected-form restoration evidence requirements, priors, headword conventions and manual choices remain separate policies.
Forms with no local inventory still accept the contextual proposal (generated-lemma acceptance is a separate, undecided question).
Unresolved context keeps the 1.0.0 GreTa helper when top-k supplies no local candidate.
counterexamples: A model-only invented lemma cannot replace the sole local σπένδω analysis of ἐσπεισάμην.
GreTa agreement does not overrule a resolved contextual disambiguation of an ambiguous form.
Morpho definition text does not establish an exact-form manually verified analysis.

Isaeus 1 Κλεωνύμου: neural-first proposals Κλείνομος, Κλεέναμος, Κλόωνυμος etc. do not replace the local Κλεώνυμος/Κλεωνύμης inventory; canonical lookup or top-k contextual decoding supplies Κλεώνυμος.

Isaeus 1.20 πλείστου: the local inventory lists πλεῖστος, not πολύς; top-k contextual decoding selects πλεῖστος (log-prob gap <= 2.5). Whether the superlative is named under πολύς is a headword-convention question for grc.lemma.diogenes-headword, not for this selection rule.

Isaeus 1.22 ἀπεχθήσεσθαι: the correct ἀπεχθάνομαι is missing from the local inventory; ἀπεχθίζομαι is an attested headword and is kept by the rescue, wrongly here. It is queued for review because it lacks a local analysis of this form.
Acharnians 263–276 Φαλῆς: the form's inventory spells Φαλής; the attested headword Φαλῆς is kept by the rescue instead of being overwritten by a deep-tail top-k script (log-prob gap > 2.5).
Acharnians 253 ἄγ' (shared-context elision): tying readings are disambiguated by contextual lemma/grammar fit so ἄγε (ἄγω) beats ἄγα (ἄγη).

sources.description: Explicit component responsibilities and GreBERTa joint replacement requested by the application owner.
Pinned joint model; neural outputs and model-owned lookups are distinct.
Owner chose the local-inventory constraint after the Isaeus 1 audit (29 contextual selections outside an available inventory) and the attested-headword rescue after the Acharnians replay.

Owner approved keep-aware script-0 decoding, cleaned resolved-only canonical_lemma, shared-context elision tie-breaking, and 1.3.0 precedence: in-inventory canonical_lemma, then top-k contextual decoding guarded by topk_known_headword_max_gap=2.5 against overriding high-confidence attested headwords, then GreTa, then attested headword rescue.

parameters.context_composition: pyaegean 0.61.0 neural-first with explicit ["keep"] script-0 handling and top-k edit-script aggregation; outside-inventory proposals check canonical lookup, then top-k contextual candidates (guarded by max gap 2.5 when top-1 is an attested headword), then GreTa, then attested local headword, then abstention

validation.scope: Provider-contract regressions; Isaeus 1 and frozen Acharnians samples are development evidence only.

rules.title: Diogenes/Morpheus headwords anchored to verified LSJ identities
conditions: Name an already selected lexical item; this policy does not choose among competing analyses.
The caller supplies verified entries from a fingerprinted local LSJ reference, separate from provider evidence.
A verified selected Morpheus association identifies its exact entry; otherwise an unambiguous exact heading or a documented correspondence is required.
Correspondences retain stable IDs, versions, source entries, conditions, counterexamples and validation status.

NFC and grave/acute presentation are supported; case variants require verified identity. Vowel-length typography is omitted in plain headword output. Other accents, breathings, diaeresis and homograph identities remain significant.
rules.effect: Return the standard headword and snapshot-qualified entry identity, or retain the original proposal with an explicit abstention. Preserve raw provider proposals and selected analysis evidence.
exceptions: Manual choices and the previously agreed separate deictic -ι headwords are retained.
Guessed, missing, mismatching or unverified Morpheus associations cannot establish canonical entry identity.
A documented alternate provider heading is not a general synonym relation; scoped mappings require the current form's verified entry.
Homographs without a selected verified identity, unavailable targets and uncovered words abstain.
A dictionary heading match verifies naming only, not the contextual or morphological analysis.
Existing OGA imports and snapshots change only through an explicit headword-standardization action or new analysis.
counterexamples: A lone καίνω candidate does not establish that κανοῦν is a verb.
Do not globally replace προσλέγω with προσεῖπον; the scoped correspondence requires a verified form association.
Do not choose an entry for homographic ἄπειμι by discarding homograph numbers.
Do not repair Χαίρις or another accented name by approximate spelling.
Do not strip -ι from νυνί or οὑτοσί.

sources.description: Owner approved Diogenes/Morpheus as the headword reference, verified LSJ anchors, documented correspondences, provisional links, uncovered words and preserved manual/deictic choices.
Diogenes packages Morpheus-generated morphology and reference dictionaries. Installed assets are fingerprinted rather than assumed identical to other versions.
Exact lexical sources and scope of every original correspondence. No third-party dictionary is included in the MIT package.

validation.scope: Portable, reference-identity, model-free workflow and frozen development-evidence checks; not independently adjudicated accuracy.

provenance.code: Original code, documentation and correspondence catalogue MIT. Installed LSJ, Morpheus tables, external annotations and model assets retain separate provenance/licences.

rules.title: Proper noun class for capitalised headwords
conditions: Apply after lemma selection and headword standardization to a machine decision whose part of speech is NOUN.
The selected lemma begins with a capital letter (the dictionary spells it as a name).
The written form also begins with a capital letter; leading apostrophes and editorial signs are ignored.
rules.effect: Return proposed_pos PROPN; morphology, lemma and provider evidence are unchanged.
exceptions: A capitalised lemma on a lower-case form abstains and is reported for review: usually a wrongly capitalised lemma (μυρρίνας -> Μυρρίνη), sometimes a personification.
Adjectives (ethnics such as Ἀθηναῖος, Λακωνικός), adverbs (Ἀθήναζε) and verbs (Μεγαρίζω) keep their class.
Manual and reviewed choices, OGA imports and previously saved decisions are outside automatic application.
counterexamples: A sentence-initial common noun: its lemma is lower case, so it stays NOUN.
A personified common noun printed in lower case (πειθώ) stays NOUN and is reported.
A wrongly capitalised lemma on a capitalised form is not detected by this rule.

sources.description: Owner chose option A after the audit of an Aristophanes project (94,761 words): 2,826 capitalised NOUN lemmata and 2 PROPN, the latter manual corrections.

sources.title: Universal Dependencies, PROPN

sources.supports: The contextual model has no PROPN label (AGDT-style training data tags names as n).

validation.scope: Isaeus 1 and an Aristophanes project; regression checks do not independently establish accuracy.

rules.title: Checks on contextual lemmata generated for forms without a local analysis
conditions: Apply after selection to a single-word form whose local (Diogenes) inventory is empty and whose lemma was generated by the contextual model; never to manual or reviewed choices.

Same word in the text: a proposal with log p <= -1.0 whose own stem does not begin the form is replaced by the single reliable lemma of the same text whose stem (citation ending removed, at least 5 letters) begins the form with at most 4 further letters and the same initial case.
Reliable lemmata: from a local analysis, a manual choice, or a generated lemma with log p > -0.5.
Impossible spelling: otherwise a proposal with two accents, an initial vowel without breathing, a final letter no Greek word ends in, or a non-letter is removed (no lemma).
rules.effect: Return proposed_lemma (replacement) or none (removal). The caller records a review observation for both; the model proposal remains in the evidence.
exceptions: Several matching reliable lemmata: no replacement.
Plausible low-confidence proposals without a matching reliable lemma are kept; generated lemmata are not otherwise judged.
The model's next candidates are not used: in a trial they were often unrelated real words (ὦναίσχυντε -> ἀγαθός).
counterexamples: Δήμητρι keeps Δημήτηρ although Δημητρίη also occurs: the proposal already fits the form.
A wrong but real word with the same stem can still be taken over (γύναικο -> γύναιον); hence the review observation.

sources.description: Owner chose removal (no lemma, review) for impossible spellings after a trial on Isaeus 1 and an Aristophanes project (961 generated lemmata; 18 same-word replacements and 128 impossible spellings).

validation.scope: Trial on Isaeus 1 and one Aristophanes project; not an accuracy measurement.
